column7: "the model calculates the ice velocity by solving a depth-integrated viscosity approximation of the Stokes equations (Goldberg, 2011)"

column18: 5000-year spin-up under 1960-1989 SMB and ST in which "the basal friction parameters are calibrated to nudge the ice surface elevation towards observed conditions following Pollard and Deconto (2012)", then "relax for an additional 1000 years, for the 4 km grid resolution"; "We assign the resulting ice sheet geometry to the beginning of 1960". ERA5-init: "one single initialization by applying SMB from the ERA5 reanalysis downscaled with MAR"; projections forced "by anomalies with respect to the annual mean SMB and ST of the reference period (1960-1989) from the same ESM"
column21: Nudged spin-up: Hybrid by rule D1. One of two initialization branches, each its own configuration (decision R1)
column22: "a power law for basal sliding based on Weertman (1957): τb = k^(-1/p) N^(q/p) ub^(1/p) ... N is the effective pressure ... The exponents are set to p = 3 and q = 1"; "Basal meltwater is removed immediately"
column28: Cascade step 2: friction depends on effective pressure N, so Budd, though R25 calls it a Weertman power law. With meltwater removed, N is probably close to the overburden pressure
